policy_title: Reset UK Government Relationship with Devolved Administrations
stated: Labour will strengthen intergovernmental working across the UK, resetting the UK government's relationship with devolved governments in Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. This includes strengthening the Sewel Convention with a new memorandum of understanding, establishing a Council of the Nations and Regions for collaboration, and ensuring members of devolved legislatures have the same free speech protections as Westminster MPs. UK-wide bodies will be made more representative, and decision-making over structural funds allocation will be restored to devolved representatives. Additional funding will be provided to Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland from UK public service investments.

source.quote: As part of Labour’s plans to clean up politics and return it to the service of working people, we will reset the UK government’s relationship with devolved governments in Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. We will strengthen the Sewel Convention by setting out a new memorandum of understanding outlining how the nations will work together for the common good. We will ensure members of devolved legislatures have the same free speech protections enjoyed by MPs at Westminster, so elected representatives can hold power to account. Labour will renew opportunities for the Prime Minister and Heads of Devolved Government to collaborate with each other. As recommended in the Report of the Commission on the UK’s future, we will establish a new Council of the Nations and Regions. This will bring together the Prime Minister, the First Ministers of Scotland and Wales, the First and deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland, and the Mayors of Combined Authorities. We will ensure that UK-wide bodies are more representative of our nations and regions. Labour will restore decision-making over the allocation of structural funds to the representatives of Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. The planned investments in public services outlined in this manifesto by a UK government will result in additional funding for Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

bearing_set.reason: The explicit commitment to grant members of devolved legislatures the same free speech (parliamentary privilege-equivalent) protections as Westminster MPs is a direct legal-rights equality matter — it addresses unequal civil-rights standing between elected representatives; restoring structural-funds decision-making to devolved representatives also touches democratic self-determination rights.

Explicitly extending the same free speech (parliamentary privilege) protections to devolved legislature members as Westminster MPs is a concrete expansion of free-expression rights for those legislators, falling squarely within O10's speech/expression indicator.

Restoring structural fund allocation decisions to devolved representatives and directing additional UK public-service investment funding to Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland is a concrete mechanism to reduce regional inequality — a core O14 indicator — beyond a marginal or incidental effect.

membership_note: The policy is primarily institutional and constitutional; its material effects on the defined fundamentals are concentrated in democratic rights/representation (O9), legislative free speech (O10), and regional inequality via structural funds and additional transfers (O14). Effects on public finances (O12) are unquantified and described as reallocation rather than new borrowing, so do not clearly clear the non-negligible bar.
